title: When the Goalposts Move
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses the specific discomfort teams experience when goals or targets change mid-stream, arguing that leaders routinely underestimate how much explanation this kind of change actually requires. The author notes that team members often interpret shifting goals as evidence that leadership was less than truthful earlier. The piece's central recommendation is that leaders must proactively supply the full context behind a goal change, treating the explanation as a two-way dialogue rather than a top-down announcement.
points: Shifting goals mid-stream is uniquely destabilizing because team members often read it as evidence leadership was less than transparent earlier.
Leaders frequently underestimate how much context a goal change requires.
If a leader doesn't have the full context behind a goal change themselves, the piece argues they're obligated to go get it.
Framing the conversation as a two-way dialogue converts reluctant compliance into genuine buy-in.
quotes: This is an uncomfortable pivot for everyone, but especially for team members who depend on goal stability to make progress.
Those below feel yanked around and often judge higher-ups as having been less truthful or implicit in the process of unnecessary change.
Leaders too often presume everyone already understands the changing conditions and the reasons for new goals. They don’t.
This is always best as a two-way dialogue. By mapping out the changing dynamics and discussing them in a give-and-take format, leaders create the context team members need.
A sudden change to targets and goals shakes people up and makes them question what they have been working so hard for.
